project_specification.project_name: nullius — guided theme roots v2: nine owner-approved themes with mechanism briefs in the authoring prompt
project_specification.addition_summary: The owner approved hypothesis space v2 on 2026-10-13 (docs/hypothesis-space/themes-v2.md; PRD 9.3 updated). Three pre-registered M2 pivots failed on the v1 set. Two reasons: - The prompt shows the agent only a theme slug. - Three v1 themes have no data in the lake. v2 has nine themes. Each carries a brief (mechanism, inputs, expected sign, notes), and five construction rules apply to every theme. This spec: - commits v2 as the legal set in both places that hold one today, and tests that the two agree (features 1 and 2) - renders the node's brief and the shared rules into the authoring prompt

existing_context.test_baseline: main at the commit carrying this spec: gate 1663 passed.
existing_context.conventions: Follow CLAUDE.md. Existing pieces, per a code map on 2026-10-13: - packages/signal-agent/src/signal_agent/legal_themes.json is the committed legal set: a policy marker plus slug/title entries. _themes.py compile_legal_themes (~:293) validates it; LegalThemes exposes slugs() and title(). The six v1 slugs differ from discovery's. - packages/discovery/src/discovery/themes.py has DEFAULT_LEGAL_THEMES (~:177), overridable by NULLIUS_LEGAL_THEMES. orchestrator/_campaign.py _themes_for plants roots round-robin over discovery.legal_themes_from_env(), so a campaign's theme_root values are discovery's slugs. - signal-agent _authoring_prompt.py: _task_part (~:432) builds the task mapping (campaign_id, theme_root, depth, contract, answer_format, cost_awareness). _render_system renders it as sorted JSON.

category.name: Hypothesis Space
category.feature: System commits the owner-approved v2 theme roots with their briefs as the signal agent's legal set, so that the committed set returns the nine v2 slugs and each theme's brief. - legal_themes.json holds the nine v2 entries, in the order and with the slugs of docs/hypothesis-space/themes-v2.md's Themes table: funding-crowding, basis-premium, oi-price-divergence, positioning-contrarian, taker-flow-persistence, low-volatility, beta-to-btc, attention-volume, intermediate-momentum. - Each entry has a title and a brief object with four non-empty strings: mechanism, inputs, expected_sign and notes. They are transcribed from that table's columns. - A top-level construction_rules list holds the doc's five shared rules, verbatim in substance. - The _comment is updated to cite PRD 9.3 v2 and the doc. - compile_legal_themes: - accepts the brief and construction_rules - refuses a malformed brief (missing key, or a non-string or blank value), or construction_rules that are not a list of non-empty strings, with ThemeSetError - treats an entry with no brief and a document with no construction_rules as legal - LegalThemes gains: - brief(slug): a mapping, or None for no brief or an unknown slug - construction_rules(): a tuple, empty when absent Existing API is unchanged. - Tests that pin a v1 slug as legal are updated to a v2 slug; each keeps its intent. Tests that pin "six" pin nine. - The signal-agent member suite passes under pytest-xdist.

System plants campaign roots in the v2 theme roots by default, so that `./run.sh campaign` returns roots whose theme_root values are the nine v2 slugs, matching the signal agent's committed set. - discovery DEFAULT_LEGAL_THEMES becomes the nine v2 slugs, in the committed order, and its docstring cites PRD 9.3 v2. NULLIUS_LEGAL_THEMES behaviour is unchanged. - discovery's test_themes.py pins the nine slugs, in the same transcribed-from-the-doc style it uses for the six today. - tests/test_theme_sets_agree.py asserts: - discovery.DEFAULT_LEGAL_THEMES equals signal_agent.committed_legal_themes().slugs(), in the same order - every committed theme has a brief It passes under pytest-xdist. - The discovery member suite and root tests/ pass.

System renders the node's theme brief and the shared construction rules in the authoring prompt, so that the model returns a signal built on the stated mechanism, inputs and expected sign of its theme. - _task_part adds a theme_brief key: the committed brief for the workspace's theme_root, read once through committed_legal_themes(). It contains mechanism, inputs, expected_sign and notes, plus construction_rules. - A theme_root with no committed brief renders theme_brief as null. This covers a v1 slug on a resumed campaign and a deployment's own NULLIUS_LEGAL_THEMES slug. It is never a refusal. - The brief also states, as one line, that expected_sign is pre-registered: a signal that flips it is a different hypothesis and must say so in its stated mechanism. - Every other rendered key and section is byte-identical to before. Existing prompt tests are updated only where they pin the task mapping's exact key set. - test_prompt_theme_brief.py covers: - for each of the nine slugs, the rendered system message contains that theme's mechanism and expected_sign, and the five rules - an unknown slug renders theme_brief null and the prompt builds - the other task keys are unchanged against a pinned rendering It passes under pytest-xdist. The signal-agent member suite passes.
